corpus_impact: None. The run wrote only to this log. No evidence_ledger entry, no fact_evidence_link, no corpus field and no seed change.
defect: probes_for() passed each entity through str() without unwrapping the [name, TYPE] pair the corpus stores, so every probe was the literal text of the pair rather than the name. No probe could match any article text.
remedy: probes_for() now unwraps pairs exactly as resource_corpus.entity_probes does. The batch was re-run; the superseding records follow this line.
what_is_invalid: Every no_prose_support_found verdict in the retracted records, and the must_match / any_of values recorded with them.
why_it_looked_like_a_result: The failure was uniform, so all 47 facts came back 'no_prose_support_found' with correct-looking titles_tried and rejected_leads fields. A 100% failure rate across a whole batch is what exposed it; a partial failure would have been far harder to see and would have read as a genuine finding about the corpus.
